tagline: Maryland's high country, from the lake to the Narrows.
intro: The byway starts high, at 2,894 feet on Keysers Ridge, and goes south by McHenry and the long shoreline of Deep Creek Lake to Oakland and its Victorian depot. From Oakland it branches toward the Savage River forest, Kitzmiller and the Allegheny Highlands, then gathers up through Lonaconing and Frostburg for the run down to Cumberland.
Deep Creek Lake is a power company's work, dammed between 1923 and 1925, with 69 miles of shoreline. The plant came on at 4 p.m. on May 26, 1925, and the state bought the lake in 2000.

moments.title: Swallow Falls
moments.text: Muddy Creek drops 53 feet in a park on the Youghiogheny under hemlocks some 300 years old. Edison, Ford and Firestone camped by the falls in the summers of 1918 and 1921.

moments.title: Cranesville Swamp
moments.text: A frost pocket on the West Virginia line that keeps a northern climate, with sundews in the sphagnum and the southernmost natural stand of American larch.

moments.title: Cumberland Narrows
moments.text: Wills Creek cuts the mountain here, and the old National Road, the railroads and the bike trail all squeeze through the gap under the quartzite cliff called Lover's Leap.
